headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and capability conflict; data leakage is limited by B's no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat (A) reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, so its outputs can be bridged into RisingWave (B) through shared files if B consumes them. B has no documented ingestion path, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly observed; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable workspace directory
IF B parses files produced by A as trusted input
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct directories
Require manual review of A-produced files before B reads them
Disable automatic file watchers on B
Use read-only mounts for B where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: A can read local files and send context to a model provider, but B is documented with no network egress and no data classes touched. That makes direct exfiltration from B unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to local workspace exposure through A.
conditions: IF B is given sensitive local files through the shared workspace
IF A is allowed to read those same files
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Run A on a minimal file subset
Use separate OS users for A and B
Audit A's prompts before sending them to the model provider

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. If B also writes to the same mutable workspace or repository, concurrent edits can clobber each other; because B's write behavior is undocumented, uncertainty escalates rather than downgrades.
conditions: IF B writes to the same repository or workspace as A
IF either agent modifies git state without external locking
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repo
Use per-agent branches
Add a lock file around write operations
Run a pre-commit diff check before merging changes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat (A) produces diff-based edit proposals, and B is a data-engineering system that could plausibly consume those outputs as authoritative instructions if wired together. No verification step is documented for the pair, so the main risk is A's output being acted on without independent validation.
conditions: IF B ingests A's proposed diffs or summaries as ground truth
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of A's outputs
Compare proposed diffs against source-of-truth inputs
Block direct execution of A-generated actions
Log and diff all downstream transformations

E_compliance.rationale: A handles model-provider API keys and source code, while B has no documented data classes or residency/compliance constraints. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore limited and only becomes relevant if regulated data is introduced into A's workspace; B is not cited further because no such obligations are documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A's file set
IF B is later connected to that same regulated dataset
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A's workspace
Document data-class boundaries for both agents
Add retention rules to the shared storage
Review vendor and residency terms before deployment
